newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian market rates steady despite weak demand.
newsitem.headline: Croatian market rates steady despite weak demand.

text.p: The Croatian interbank rates were unchanged despite weaker demand on Tuesday and dealers said it will take at least two weeks before the market reacts by cutting prices.
"This is only a short improvement which will not result in decline of price as yet," one dealer told Reuters.
Market's liquidity improved last week after central bank's intervention and repayments to banks by the pension fund.
Morning settlements were modest at 14.7 million kuna, mostly in call money deals struck at 10.5 percent and one 1.7 million loan made at 11 percent.
There was 30 million surplus in supply, but 1.5 million kuna sought by savings banks found no lenders.
Creditors charged 14 percent for two-week funds and 15 percent for one-month money.
Overnight trade on Monday reached 113.8 million kuna, mostly used for mandatory reserves and only 3.8 million sought by banks with shortfalls. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
